# Exact environment that produced the frozen results

**Generated by `scripts/23_export_environment.py`. Every value below was read
from the running interpreter, not written from memory.** Regenerate with
`python scripts/23_export_environment.py --write`.

This file exists because of A9: the NSCLC ISI is 0.318240180054566 on this
platform and 0.2964 on Linux/x86_64 with the same pinned versions and
byte-identical inputs. A reader who reproduces a different number needs to be
able to tell whether they are seeing A9 or their own setup drift. Comparing
against this file is how.

## Threading

**No BLAS thread-count variable is set for macOS runs, deliberately.** Thread
count changes floating-point reduction order, and A9 *is* a numerical
reproducibility investigation, so the environment is kept identical to the one
that produced the frozen results. The cluster sbatch scripts DO set them;
cluster numbers are diagnostic, never manuscript numbers.

Observed at generation time:

| variable | value |
|---|---|
| `OMP_NUM_THREADS` | (unset) |
| `VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS` | (unset) |
| `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS` | (unset) |
| `MKL_NUM_THREADS` | (unset) |
| `PYTHONHASHSEED` | (unset) |

`PYTHONHASHSEED=0` is exported by `reproduce.sh`, because str hashing is
randomised per process and gene-pool ordering must be deterministic. If it
reads `(unset)` above, this file was generated outside `reproduce.sh` -- that
does not affect any other value, but it is why the row is printed rather than
assumed.

## Seed audit

Every source of randomness in the pipeline, and where its seed is set.
**Re-derived 2026-09-05 by reading every call site, not by grep.** The previous
version of this table was written from a grep and listed four sources; there are
**twelve** `np.random.default_rng` call sites in `src/aacr27/`. All twelve are
deterministic, but six of them were undocumented and four take their seed from a
DEFAULT ARGUMENT rather than from `AuditConfig`, which is a weaker guarantee than
this table used to imply: they agree with the configured seed because
`seed: int = 0` happens to match `AuditConfig.seed = 0`, not because anything
wires them together. Changing `AuditConfig.seed` would silently NOT change them.

| source | call site | seeded by | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| null gene-set draws | `signatures.py:353` | `AuditConfig.seed` (0) | per-signature nulls deliberately SHARE the seed, so two signatures of identical size and expression profile draw identical sets. Intentional for the family-level statistic; it means the 16 nulls are not independent (Limitations 7). |
| patient-clustered bootstrap | `stats.py:97` | `AuditConfig.seed` (0) | one patient set resampled per draw and shared across signatures, preserving between-signature correlation. |
| pooled-ISI bootstrap | `experiment.py:944` | `config.seed`, explicit | the pooled interval; passed the config directly. |
| Δr split-robustness bootstrap | `stats.py:135` | `config.seed`, explicit at `experiment.py:448` | `paired_delta`. Previously undocumented. |
| site-to-fold partition | `splits.py:171`, and `splits.py:64` for the stratified path | `AuditConfig.fold_seed` | a derived property, not a field: `experiment.py:137` returns `self.seed if self.split_seed is None else self.split_seed`, so the partition follows `seed` **unless** `split_seed` is set. Varied ONLY by `12_partition_variance.py`, which holds `seed` fixed so the spread it reports is attributable to the partition and nothing else. **The seed is not the whole story here — see A9 below.** |
| split-half reliability | `signatures.py:643` | explicit at `13_scorer_sensitivity.py:272`; default `seed=0` | the scorer-agnostic reliability used by A7's reconstruction. Previously undocumented. |
| Control C permutation calibration | `decomposition.py:393` | **DEFAULT `seed=0` only** — `11_close_science_gaps.py:177` passes no seed | deterministic, but not wired to `AuditConfig`. Previously undocumented. |
| ancestry Cramér's V calibration | `ancestry.py:127` | **DEFAULT `seed=0` only** — `06_run_ancestry.py:93` passes no seed | the identifiability result in Supplementary Table S1. Previously undocumented. |
| ancestry pooling | `ancestry.py:341` | **DEFAULT `seed=0` only** | Previously undocumented. |
| rotation null | *(no RNG)* | — | `stats.py:232` **consumes no randomness at all**: it reuses the already-drawn `null_r` matrix and computes a permutation p from it. The previous table listed it as "`AuditConfig.seed` (0), 1,000 draws", which was true of the draws it reads but wrong about the function, which is a pure transformation of its input. |
| str hashing / gene-pool order | — | `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` | exported by `reproduce.sh`. NOT set by default in an interactive shell -- see the table above. |

**What is NOT seeded, and does not need to be:** the ridge solve and
`scipy.stats.pearsonr` are deterministic given their inputs. That is precisely
why A9 is interesting -- with every seed pinned and the inputs hashed
identical, the answer still moves across platforms.

## Sort stability -- the determinism surface this file used to miss

**This document described threading and seeds as the determinism surface. The
actual determinism failures were neither.** Both were non-stable sorts. A seed
audit cannot find them, because they do not consume randomness at all: with
every seed pinned and every input hashed identical, `np.argsort`'s default
`kind="quicksort"` orders exactly-tied keys by an implementation-defined rule,
and numpy ships different SIMD kernels for arm64 and x86_64 that disagree.

| site | what ties | fixed | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `splits.py:177` | 51 of 68 NSCLC site sizes | `kind="stable"`, 2026-09-05 | A9. Fold hash `e55ee4e8887b5167` (macOS) vs `a40c862b12d9a391` (HPC4) before; `9f31e33c2caaf1e3` on both after. 216 patients moved fold; now 0. |
| `signatures.py:212` | 35,394,448 of 38,747,424 rank entries, all 944 samples | `kind="stable"`, 2026-09-05 | A10. Depth hash `0bca973cfa26da89` (macOS) vs `b98fb11e701e8e98` (HPC4) under quicksort; `096172c056cc7a34` on both under stable. ssGSEA scores moved by 0.61 of a score sd. |
| `stats.py:180` | tied *p*-values | not needed | BH assigns tied *p* the same *q* whichever order they take. Forced all-tied families give max abs delta-q = 0. |
| `barcodes.py:130` | 51 tied site counts | not needed | `site_summary` is never called. Re-measured by grep on every audit run. |
| `models.py:339` | 0 of 15 site AUROCs | not needed | consumed only through a median. |
| `outcome.py:173,181` | -- | already `kind="stable"` | deliberate, predates the audit. |

**Two things follow for anyone extending this pipeline.** First, a new
`np.argsort`, `sort_values`, or `nlargest` on a key that can tie is a
reproducibility change, not a style choice -- pass `kind="stable"` unless you
have measured that ties cannot occur. Second, the guards that exist are cheap
and they fail: `scripts/24_split_determinism.py --check` (~3 s) and
`scripts/26_sort_audit.py` (~28 s, `--deep` ~95 s) both exit 1 if a fix is
reverted, both are wired into `reproduce.sh`, and both carry a `--self-test`
that is checked in **both** directions -- it must fire on tie-heavy input and
stay quiet on tie-free input, because a comparison that always differs is as
useless as one that never does.

## The second platform, in full

The frozen results were produced on the macOS row. HPC4 is recorded here because
the cheapest evidence a reader can check for the sort-stability claims above is
the two-platform diff, and until 2026-09-05 that record existed only inside a
job log. Measured, not transcribed: `20_check_versions.py` and
`23_export_environment.py` on each machine, plus cluster job 121782.

| | macOS (frozen results) | Einstein HPC4 |
|---|---|---|
| system / arch | Darwin 15, arm64 | Linux, x86_64 (node cpu-850) |
| Python | 3.13.9 | 3.12.14 |
| BLAS | openblas 0.3.21 | scipy-openblas 0.3.27 |
| numpy / pandas | 2.1.3 / 2.2.3 | 2.1.3 / 2.2.3 |
| scikit-learn / scipy | 1.6.1 / 1.15.3 | 1.6.1 / 1.15.3 |

The package versions are identical and the Python and BLAS builds are not, which
is what makes the pair useful: it isolates architecture and interpreter from
library version. **BLAS is reported here, not gated** by `20_check_versions.py`,
and A9/A10 are the evidence that this is the right call -- BLAS was suspected
for six sessions and eliminated by measurement (a job run at 1 and 8 threads on
one node was bit-identical), while the real cause was a sort in pure numpy.
